messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: All-in-One Digital Microfluidic Pipeline for Automated Proteomic Sample Processing -- Plasma Metabolite Extraction and Two-Step Chemical Derivatization for Comprehensive Two-Dimensional Gas Chromatography Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry (GCxGC-TOFMS) Biomarker Discovery

REAGENTS USED:
  - Plasma Sample (100 uL room-temperature plasma from EDTA-collected, clotted, and centrifuged whole blood)
  - Extraction Solvent (900 uL methanol:water, 8:1 v/v)
  - Methoxyamine Reagent (20 mg/mL methoxyamine hydrochloride in ACS grade pyridine, 30 uL aliquot)
  - MSTFA + TMCS Reagent (N-methyl-N-(trimethylsilyl)trifluoroacetamide with 1% trimethylchlorosilane, 70 uL aliquot)

STEPS:
1. Extraction: Combine the 100 uL plasma sample with 900 uL methanol:water (8:1 v/v) extraction solvent in a microcentrifuge tube.
2. Cool/homogenize/cool: Cool the mixture on ice for 10 min, homogenize by vortex mixing for 10 min, then cool again on ice for 10 min prior to centrifugation and transfer of the supernatant.
3. Pre-derivatization drying: Dry the transferred extract using a SpeedVac for 40 min immediately prior to the first derivatization step to ensure no residual water is present.
4. First derivatization (methoximation): Add a 30 uL aliquot of methoxyamine hydrochloride/pyridine solution to the dried extract and incubate at 30 C for 90 min with the vial capped.
5. Second derivatization (silylation): Add a 70 uL aliquot of MSTFA + 0.1% TMCS solution to the methoximated extract and incubate at 60 C for 90 min.
6. Detection: Inject the derivatized extract onto the GCxGC-TOFMS instrument (reverse column configuration) and acquire full-scan mass spectra (m/z 33-500) for downstream Fisher-ratio and control-normalized Fisher-ratio biomarker analysis, then discard the analyzed extract.

INTERPRETATION: Successful automated sample processing is confirmed when the resulting chromatographic data reproduce the metabolite/biomarker hit lists (e.g., succinic acid, arachidonic acid, L-methionine, and other patient-vs-control discriminating metabolites) obtained via standard and control-normalized Fisher-ratio analysis, with signal reproducibility and concentration ratios consistent across replicate extraction/derivatization batches, supporting the feasibility of an automated, all-in-one digital microfluidic pipeline for proteomic/metabolomic sample preparation upstream of GCxGC-TOFMS biomarker discovery.

module fluorescence

manifest plasma_sample
manifest extraction_solvent
manifest methoxyamine_reagent
manifest mstfa_tmcs_reagent

instructions:

plasma = dispense 100 units of plasma_sample
solvent = dispense 900 units of extraction_solvent
extract = mix plasma with solvent for 600s

heat extract at 4c for 10m
heat extract at 25c for 10m
heat extract at 4c for 10m

heat extract at 25c for 40m

derivatize1 = dispense 30 units of methoxyamine_reagent
step1 = mix extract with derivatize1
heat step1 at 30c for 90m

derivatize2 = dispense 70 units of mstfa_tmcs_reagent
step2 = mix step1 with derivatize2
heat step2 at 60c for 90m

metabolite_reading = detect fluorescence on step2 for 300s

dispose step2

metadata.protocol_name: All-in-One Digital Microfluidic Pipeline for Automated Proteomic Sample Processing (Venkatesh et al., Anal. Chem. 2020)

sources.title: All-in-One Digital Microfluidic Pipeline for Automated Proteomic Sample Processing

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's plasma extraction and two-step chemical derivatization procedure (Supporting Information, 'Experimental details'), covering methanol:water extraction, ice-cooling/vortex-homogenization/ice-cooling, pre-derivatization SpeedVac drying, methoximation with methoxyamine/pyridine, silylation with MSTFA + TMCS, and final GCxGC-TOFMS injection. Because BioScript has no primitive for centrifugation, supernatant transfer, or vacuum evaporation, these physical separation/drying steps are approximated using 'heat' calls at nominal temperatures/durations rather than dedicated operations. Likewise, because the paper's detection modality is full-scan GCxGC-TOFMS acquisition (not a fluorogenic readout), the 'detect fluorescence' primitive is used as a stand-in for the generic detect-and-quantify step, representing the mass-spectral signal acquisition rather than an actual fluorescence measurement, since BioScript's grammar does not expose a dedicated chromatography/mass-spectrometry detect module.

numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript has no dedicated vortex or centrifugation primitive, so the 10 min vortex-homogenization step is modeled as a 'heat' call at a nominal room temperature (25c) rather than an actual mechanical mixing operation; the two 10 min ice-cooling steps are modeled as 'heat' at 4c.

The paper specifies SpeedVac vacuum evaporation, not simple heating; no vacuum-evaporation primitive exists in BioScript, so a nominal room-temperature 'heat' call is used to represent the stated 40 min drying duration. The initial post-extraction evaporation-to-dryness step (duration/temperature not explicitly stated in the paper) is not separately modeled.

numeric_mismatches.field: centrifugation steps (1300g and 15000g) and supernatant transfer
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. BioScript has no centrifugation or liquid-transfer-between-vessels primitive; the extract is treated as a single continuous droplet from mixing through derivatization and detection.

Detection in the paper is GCxGC-TOFMS full-scan mass spectrometric acquisition (m/z 33-500, 100 spectra/s) feeding into Fisher-ratio and control-normalized Fisher-ratio statistical analysis, not a fluorogenic bulk signal. 'detect fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect module exposed by BioScript's grammar.

numeric_mismatches.field: GCxGC oven/modulation program, Fisher-ratio/control-normalized Fisher-ratio statistical workflow (Figures S1-S2), PCA analysis (Figure S3), metabolite standard-mix spiking procedure (Table S1), and per-metabolite bin-size/%RSD signal-distribution analysis (Table S4)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are instrument chromatographic-method parameters, downstream chemometric/statistical analysis workflows, and characterization sub-experiments run on the resulting data, not part of the core sample-preparation protocol itself, and fall outside the scope of this translation; only the extraction and two-step derivatization procedure is captured here.
